collection: Marland on Wilde - facsimiles from the list of uncollected letters

archive.name: Various - auction houses, dealers and library catalogues
archive.page_id_note: Not an archive. `pointer` is a scraped filename and is NOT unique - 16 of them repeat across items, img-00.jpg among them - so it cannot be a key.

purpose: A finding aid, not an archive: letters the Complete Letters never printed, gathered from a blog that indexes them. None is quoted in web/data.
rights_note: Per-image and mostly unresolved - largely auction-house photography. Not for republication; recorded as UND.
notes: Per-page `file` is relative to `../../manuscripts/<key>/`, the private tree that holds the images. The path is metadata; the images are what stays unpublished.

Images were triaged by eye on contact sheets. Removed: site chrome (auction-house logos, social buttons, trust seals, category banners, a placeholder graphic, a staff headshot); photographs of unrelated lots in the same sale (a Rolex, a Montblanc pen set, a Fornasetti plate, German-hand letters by other writers); two uniform-white PNGs; and lower-resolution rescales of an image kept elsewhere in the same folder, identified by per-pixel agreement rather than a perceptual hash, which had grouped sibling pages of one letter as duplicates. Kept but labelled in `context`: images about the letter rather than of it - a portrait of the recipient, a newspaper clipping, the book it was laid into, the framed lot as it hung, and listing screenshots in folders where nothing better was captured. `n_facsimile` counts the images that are pages of the letter.

No `printed` pointers here, and there cannot be. This is the list of uncollected letters - letters the Complete Letters do not contain - so there is no folio in that volume to cite for any of the 97. That is the whole reason the collection exists and is not an omission. Where an item carries `matches`, the entry names a person the letter was written to who is on the map, not a source that quotes it.
`items` was `letter_folders` before the manifests were brought into one shape; one item per letter, `pointer` is the image filename.
A page marked `is_context` is about the letter rather than of it - a portrait, a clipping, the framed lot - and `n_facsimile` counts the rest.
`archive.record_url` and `iiif_url` are empty on purpose: there is no single holding archive and no image service, so this manifest can never back a `facsimile`.

A `matches` entry carries only structured facts: `pages`, `what`, `printed` {work, locator} and, where there is no printed pointer, `person`. Prose about why an entry matters lives in this archive's README, not here - the manifest restates neither the connection nor the commentary.
